data.title: Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma) — viva
data.summary: Connective tissue diseases · 30 viva questions with answers
data.body:
_Viva questions for the case: **Systemic sclerosis (scleroderma)** (Connective tissue diseases)_

**Q1. Classify scleroderma (PYQ).**
- Localised scleroderma (morphoea) — skin ± underlying tissue, no internal organ disease: plaque, generalised, linear (including en coup de sabre and Parry–Romberg), deep, pansclerotic, mixed
- Systemic sclerosis (SSc): limited cutaneous (lcSSc — skin thickening distal to elbows/knees ± face; includes CREST), diffuse cutaneous (dcSSc — proximal limbs and trunk), SSc sine scleroderma (internal disease + antibodies without skin thickening), overlap syndromes
- Scleroderma-like disorders: scleredema, scleromyxoedema, nephrogenic systemic fibrosis, eosinophilic fasciitis, chronic GVHD, porphyria cutanea tarda, phenylketonuria, drug/toxin-induced (bleomycin, taxanes, vinyl chloride, silica, toxic oil, L-tryptophan)

**Q2. Explain the pathogenesis.**
- Triad: vasculopathy (endothelial injury → intimal proliferation, obliteration, Raynaud's, ischaemia) + immune activation (autoantibodies, T/B cells, IL-6, type I IFN) + fibrosis (TGF-β, PDGF, CTGF → myofibroblasts producing excess collagen in skin and organs)

**Q3. Describe skin features.**
- Raynaud's phenomenon (first symptom in >90%)
- Oedematous (puffy fingers) → indurated → atrophic phases
- Sclerodactyly (tapered, tight, shiny fingers with flexion contractures), digital pitting scars, ulcers on fingertips and knuckles, resorption of terminal phalanges (acro-osteolysis)
- Face: mask-like expressionless face, beaked nose, microstomia with radial perioral furrowing (purse-string mouth), loss of wrinkles
- Salt-and-pepper pigmentation (perifollicular retention with depigmentation), telangiectasias (matted), calcinosis cutis, nailfold capillary changes, pruritus (early)

**Q4. Write a short note on Raynaud's phenomenon (PYQ).**
- Episodic vasospasm of digital arteries on exposure to cold/stress — triphasic colour change: white (ischaemia/pallor) → blue (cyanosis) → red (reactive hyperaemia), with pain/numbness
- Primary (Raynaud's disease — young women, symmetrical, no ulcers, normal nailfold capillaries, ANA negative) vs secondary (SSc, SLE, MCTD, DM, Sjögren's, cryoglobulinaemia, vibration tools, thoracic outlet, drugs — β-blockers, ergots)
- Treatment: keep warm, gloves, stop smoking; calcium channel blockers (nifedipine SR, amlodipine) first line; losartan, fluoxetine, topical nitrates, PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil, tadalafil), IV iloprost, bosentan (prevents new digital ulcers), botulinum toxin, sympathectomy

**Q5. Write a short note on CREST syndrome (PYQ).**
- Limited cutaneous SSc variant: Calcinosis cutis, Raynaud's phenomenon, oEsophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia (mat-like on face, hands)
- Anti-centromere antibodies (~50–90%); slower course; late complications — pulmonary arterial hypertension, primary biliary cholangitis

**Q6. Write a short note on calcinosis cutis (PYQ).**
- Deposition of insoluble calcium salts in skin
- Types: dystrophic (normal calcium/phosphate; damaged tissue — SSc, DM, lupus, tumours, trauma), metastatic (high Ca × P product — CKD, hyperparathyroidism, hypervitaminosis D, milk-alkali), idiopathic (scrotal calcinosis, subepidermal calcified nodule, tumoral calcinosis), iatrogenic (calcium gluconate extravasation, EEG paste), calciphylaxis (vascular calcification in CKD — painful necrosis, high mortality)
- Treatment: treat cause; diltiazem, bisphosphonates, warfarin (low dose), probenecid, colchicine (inflammation), sodium thiosulphate, excision, CO2 laser, lithotripsy

**Q7. What are the systemic features?**
- GI (90%): oesophageal dysmotility (dysphagia, reflux, Barrett's), watermelon stomach (GAVE), small bowel bacterial overgrowth, pseudo-obstruction, wide-mouthed colonic diverticula, faecal incontinence
- Lungs: interstitial lung disease (leading cause of death — dcSSc, anti-Scl-70), pulmonary arterial hypertension (lcSSc, anti-centromere)
- Kidney: scleroderma renal crisis — sudden hypertension, AKI, microangiopathic haemolysis (dcSSc, anti-RNA polymerase III, high-dose steroids >15 mg/day) — ACE inhibitors are life-saving
- Heart: myocardial fibrosis, arrhythmias, pericarditis
- Musculoskeletal: tendon friction rubs (dcSSc — poor prognosis), arthralgia, myopathy; also sicca, hypothyroidism, erectile dysfunction

**Q8. Antibodies and their associations.**
- Anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70): dcSSc, ILD
- Anti-centromere: lcSSc/CREST, PAH, digital loss
- Anti-RNA polymerase III: rapid diffuse skin, renal crisis, cancer association (synchronous)
- Anti-U3 RNP (fibrillarin): PAH, myositis, young men of African descent
- Anti-PM/Scl: overlap with myositis; anti-Th/To: lcSSc with ILD/PAH

**Q9. Give the 2013 ACR/EULAR classification criteria.**
- Skin thickening of fingers of both hands extending proximal to MCP joints — sufficient alone (9 points)
- Otherwise add: skin thickening of fingers — puffy fingers 2 or sclerodactyly distal to MCP 4 (higher counted); fingertip lesions — digital ulcers 2 or pitting scars 3; telangiectasia 2; abnormal nailfold capillaries 2; PAH and/or ILD 2; Raynaud's 3; SSc-related antibodies (anti-centromere, Scl-70, RNA pol III) 3
- Total ≥9 = definite SSc (excludes scleroderma-like disorders)

**Q10. Investigations in SSc.**
- ANA (nucleolar/centromere/speckled), specific antibodies; nailfold capillaroscopy (giant capillaries, haemorrhages, avascular areas — 'scleroderma pattern': early, active, late)
- HRCT chest, PFT with DLCO, 6-minute walk, echocardiography ± right-heart catheterisation for PAH, NT-proBNP
- Renal function, BP, urine; upper GI endoscopy/manometry; skin score (modified Rodnan skin score, 17 sites 0–3, max 51)

**Q11. Management of SSc (organ-based).**
- Skin: methotrexate, mycophenolate (first choice for dcSSc skin + ILD), cyclophosphamide, rituximab, IVIG, autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplant for rapidly progressive dcSSc; physiotherapy
- Raynaud's/digital ulcers: as above (CCB, PDE5i, iloprost, bosentan)
- ILD: mycophenolate, cyclophosphamide, tocilizumab (anti-IL-6R), nintedanib (antifibrotic), rituximab, lung transplant
- PAH: endothelin receptor antagonists (bosentan, ambrisentan, macitentan), PDE5 inhibitors, prostacyclin analogues, riociguat
- Renal crisis: ACE inhibitor (captopril) titrated quickly, dialysis; avoid high-dose steroids
- GI: PPIs, prokinetics, rotating antibiotics for bacterial overgrowth
- Calcinosis and telangiectasia: as above; pulsed-dye laser for telangiectasia

**Q12. Prognosis.**
- 10-year survival ~70%; dcSSc worse; deaths mainly from ILD, PAH, cardiac disease; renal crisis mortality reduced by ACE inhibitors

**Q13. How do you examine a patient with suspected SSc (clinical case approach)?**
- Hands: puffy fingers, sclerodactyly, digital pits/ulcers/gangrene, calcinosis, flexion contractures, nailfold capillaries (hand lens/dermoscope), resorbed tips, tendon friction rubs
- Face: microstomia (measure inter-incisor distance), radial furrows, beaked nose, mat telangiectasia, salt-and-pepper pigmentation, expressionless face
- Skin score: modified Rodnan skin score (17 sites, 0–3); proximal extent decides limited vs diffuse
- Systemic: BP (renal crisis), chest (basal 'velcro' crackles — ILD; loud P2 — PAH), dysphagia, reflux, joint contractures, muscle weakness

**Q14. Describe the modified Rodnan skin score.**
- Skin thickness by palpation (0 normal, 1 mild, 2 moderate, 3 severe — cannot pinch) at 17 sites: fingers, hands, forearms, upper arms, thighs, legs, feet (bilateral) + face, anterior chest, abdomen; maximum 51; used to classify and monitor dcSSc (peaks in first 3–5 years then softens)

**Q15. What is nailfold capillaroscopy and its patterns?**
- Non-invasive examination of nailfold capillaries (videocapillaroscopy/ dermoscope with oil)
- Scleroderma pattern (Cutolo): early — few giant capillaries and haemorrhages, preserved density; active — many giant capillaries and haemorrhages, moderate loss; late — severe capillary loss, avascular areas, ramified/bushy capillaries
- Useful to differentiate primary vs secondary Raynaud's and predict progression to SSc

**Q16. What is scleroderma renal crisis — features and treatment?**
- Abrupt onset of severe hypertension (sometimes normotensive), acute kidney injury, microangiopathic haemolytic anaemia, thrombocytopenia, headache, retinopathy, pulmonary oedema; usually within 4 years of dcSSc; risk — anti-RNA polymerase III, rapidly progressive skin, prednisolone >15 mg/day
- Treatment: ACE inhibitor (captopril titrated quickly) even if creatinine rising, add CCB/ARB for BP, dialysis if needed (renal recovery possible over 2 years); avoid nephrotoxins; monitor BP at home

**Q17. Discuss digital ulcer management.**
- Prevention: stop smoking, keep warm, CCB, PDE5 inhibitors (sildenafil/tadalafil), bosentan for recurrent ulcers (prevents new ulcers)
- Active ulcers: IV iloprost (prostacyclin analogue) 3–5 days, PDE5 inhibitors, analgesia, wound care (moist dressings), treat infection (osteomyelitis risk), digital sympathectomy/ botulinum toxin, fat grafting; amputation for gangrene

**Q18. Explain the pathogenesis of oesophageal involvement.**
- Smooth-muscle atrophy and fibrosis of the lower two-thirds of oesophagus with neural damage → hypomotility, incompetent lower oesophageal sphincter → reflux, heartburn, dysphagia, strictures, Barrett's oesophagus, aspiration (worsens ILD); manometry shows absent peristalsis; treat with PPIs, prokinetics, head-end elevation, small meals

**Q19. Interstitial lung disease in SSc — screening and treatment.**
- Commonest cause of SSc-related death; risk — dcSSc, anti-Scl-70, African descent; screen all at diagnosis with HRCT and PFT (FVC, DLCO), then PFT every 6–12 months
- HRCT: NSIP pattern (ground glass with reticulation, basal), UIP less often
- Treatment: mycophenolate (SLS-II), cyclophosphamide (SLS-I), tocilizumab (early progressive), rituximab, nintedanib (antifibrotic — slows FVC decline), lung transplant

**Q20. What is pulmonary arterial hypertension in SSc?**
- Late complication of lcSSc (anti-centromere), progressive dyspnoea, loud P2, right heart failure; screening annually with echo, PFT (DLCO/FVC ratio), NT-proBNP (DETECT algorithm); right heart catheterisation (mPAP >20 mmHg, PVR >2 WU) confirms; treat with ERA + PDE5i combination, prostacyclins, riociguat; poor prognosis

**Q21. What is eosinophilic fasciitis (Shulman syndrome)?**
- Scleroderma-like disorder: acute symmetrical painful swelling then induration of limbs (sparing hands/face and fingers), peau d'orange, groove sign (venous furrows on elevating limb), after strenuous exercise; peripheral eosinophilia, hypergammaglobulinaemia; no Raynaud's; full-thickness biopsy to fascia/ MRI shows fascial thickening
- Treatment: prednisolone ± methotrexate; associated haematological disorders (aplastic anaemia) occasionally

**Q22. Name other scleroderma mimics and how to differentiate.**
- Scleredema (Buschke) — diabetes/post-streptococcal/ paraprotein; upper back and neck woody induration, no Raynaud's
- Scleromyxoedema — paraproteinaemia (IgG-λ), waxy papules, 'Shar-Pei' sign, doughnut sign on knuckles, systemic (dermato-neuro syndrome); IVIG
- Nephrogenic systemic fibrosis — gadolinium in renal failure, limbs, brawny induration
- Chronic sclerodermoid GVHD, porphyria cutanea tarda (sclerodermoid), POEMS, phenylketonuria, stiff skin syndrome, morphoea

**Q23. What are the newer and future treatments in SSc?**
- Autologous haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for early rapidly progressive dcSSc with poor prognosis (SCOT, ASTIS trials — improved survival, treatment-related mortality risk)
- Rituximab, tocilizumab (anti-IL-6R), abatacept, JAK inhibitors, nintedanib, anti-fibrotic research (lenabasum failed); CAR-T cell therapy (CD19) in refractory SSc — early reports

**Q24. Describe musculoskeletal involvement.**
- Arthralgia, synovitis, tendon friction rubs (leathery creak over tendons — dcSSc, poor prognosis), flexion contractures, acro-osteolysis (resorption of distal phalanges), calcinosis, myopathy/myositis (overlap with anti-PM/Scl, anti-Ku)

**Q25. What is the prognosis by subtype?**
- dcSSc: 10-year survival ~50–70%; early (first 5 years) high risk of renal crisis, ILD, myocardial involvement
- lcSSc: slower course, 10-year survival ~70–90%; late PAH and GI complications

**Q26. Raynaud's phenomenon — primary versus secondary (table).**
- Primary: young women, symmetrical, mild, no ulcers/pitting, normal nailfold capillaries, ANA negative, normal ESR
- Secondary: older onset (>30 y), asymmetric, severe, painful, digital ulcers/gangrene, abnormal capillaroscopy, ANA/SSc antibodies, raised ESR, features of CTD

**Q27. What are the cutaneous signs of SSc on dermoscopy and imaging?**
- Dermoscopy/ capillaroscopy as above; high-frequency ultrasound for skin thickness; plain X-ray hands — calcinosis, acro-osteolysis; thermography for Raynaud's

**Q28. Describe mixed / overlap syndromes involving SSc.**
- SSc–myositis overlap (anti-PM/Scl, anti-Ku), SSc–SLE, SSc–RA, SSc–Sjögren's, MCTD (anti-U1-RNP); management targets the dominant organ involvement

**Q29. Counselling points for an SSc patient.**
- Chronic disease with organ-based screening (yearly echo/PFT), stop smoking, protect hands from cold (gloves, warm clothes), skin care with emollients, physiotherapy/stretching to prevent contractures, oral hygiene/dental care (microstomia), small meals for reflux, home BP monitoring in dcSSc, pregnancy planning when disease stable (avoid in early dcSSc)

**Q30. What drugs/toxins cause scleroderma-like disease?**
- Bleomycin, taxanes (docetaxel), gemcitabine, pentazocine (injection-site fibrosis), vitamin K injections (Texier's disease), appetite suppressants, L-tryptophan (eosinophilia–myalgia syndrome), toxic oil syndrome (rapeseed oil), vinyl chloride, silica (Erasmus syndrome), organic solvents, epoxy resins, checkpoint inhibitors

## Quick spotter facts
- Sclerodactyly + microstomia + salt-and-pepper pigmentation — SSc
- Anti-Scl-70 → ILD; anti-centromere → CREST/PAH; anti-RNA pol III → renal crisis
- Renal crisis — ACE inhibitor

_Sources: Previous-year PG question papers (Sahana P Raju, Solved Papers Dermatology); IADVL Textbook of Dermatology 5e (Scleroderma); 2013 ACR/EULAR SSc classification criteria. Answers written in our own words; check with your teachers' preferences._
